title_en.v1.title: Homemade Masala Tofu from Soybeans: Soy Milk, Vinegar Coagulation and Pressing
title_en.v1.reason: Transcript gives the full process from soaked soybeans to pressed tofu.

detailed_summary.v3.overview: The video makes roughly half a kilo of masala tofu from 250 g soybeans. Soybeans are soaked 8–10 hours, optionally dehulled, blended with about 1.5 liters total water and strained repeatedly to extract soy milk. The milk is boiled and stirred, optionally seasoned with cumin, chili flakes, green chili, ginger, coriander and salt, then cooled slightly below boiling before gradual addition of a vinegar solution. Once curdled, the mixture rests 10–15 minutes, is strained in cloth and pressed under weight for about one hour. The finished tofu is presented as a low-cost dairy-free protein option. The leftover soybean pulp is also suggested for dough or other uses.
